children: Genentech unit on Thursday announced a late-stage trial success for a combination regimen containing its bispecific antibody, Lunsumio, against a hematological cancer known as follicular lymphoma.
The company said Lunsumio with lenalidomide, a cancer drug marketed by Bristol Myers
as Revlimid, reached the primary endpoint of its Phase 3 CELESTIMO study, indicating statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival.

The findings on overall survival were immature at the time of the interim analysis, Genentech said, adding that there were no new safety signals and the experimental regimen indicated a tolerability profile consistent with the established safety profiles of individual drugs.

CELESTIMO enrolled patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma who have received one or more prior lines of systemic therapy to evaluate lenalidomide plus Lunsumio versus lenalidomide plus Rituxan, a lymphoma drug marketed by Biogen

It was designed as a confirmatory study for Lunsumio to obtain an indication in second-line or later FL and convert its accelerated approval/conditional marketing authorization to full approval in third-line or later FL.
Lunsumio is already available in the U.S. for adults with follicular lymphoma who have received two or more prior lines of therapy.
The company plans to present the study data at an upcoming medical event and submit the results

title: Roche succeeds in late-stage study for Lunsumio regimen in follicular lymphoma
